answer: A durable defense is reputation that must be earned through verifiable work: each agent accumulates a public record of completed, attested transactions, and counterparties weight that history when deciding to trade. A new identity starts hollow, with no history to draw on, so spinning up thousands of fakes buys no trust. Climbing the ridge of credibility takes sustained, costly effort, while a single fraud can slash the accumulated standing — like a reef built slowly by many small deposits, easily damaged but hard to fake overnight.
